chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurarah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar from Kathir al-Nawwa' from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The ship was anchored - on the Day of Ashura - on al-Judi, so Noah (peace be upon him) ordered those with him from the jinn and humans to fast that day.

And Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know what this day is? This is the day on which Allah, Exalted and Majestic, accepted repentance from Adam and Hawwa (peace be upon her); and this is the day on which Allah split the sea for the Children of Israel, so He drowned Pharaoh and those with him; and this is the day on which Musa (peace be upon him) conquered Pharaoh; and this is the day on which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born; and this is the day on which Allah accepted repentance from the people of Yunus (peace be upon him); and this is the day on which Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) was born; and this is the day on which the Qa'im (peace be upon him) will rise.'
As for what has been narrated regarding the dislike of fasting on it, it has been narrated.

key_terms.الْجُودِيِّ: Al-Judi (the mountain where Noah's ship rested)
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَاشُورَاءَ: The Day of Ashura (10th of Muharram)

ai.seo_question: What are the historical and theological reasons for the significance of the Day of Ashura in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the cosmic significance of the 10th of Muharram by linking it to major salvific events in Islamic history, such as the repentance of Adam, the victory over Pharaoh, and the births of Ibrahim and Isa. This multiplicity of auspicious occasions underscores the day's unique status, explaining the scholarly debate between those who recommend fasting to commemorate these blessings and those who caution against it to avoid resembling other traditions.
